title: Too vague to pick any pattern: ask before drawing
reference: Draws nothing. Asks one or two questions whose answers decide the pattern (what the company wants to run, who uses it), each with 2-4 quick-reply options such as a website, internal systems, data and analytics, an AI assistant.

turns.ask: We need cloud for our company.

title: Online store with missing details: draw first, assume, ask at most two
reference: A complete first diagram straight away (users, edge protection, load balancer, compute, database, object storage, monitoring) in Singapore or another sensible default region. Up to three assumptions shown as chips (public-facing, region, scale) and at most two questions with quick-reply options, for example where the shoppers are.

turns.ask: Build a web app for our online store.

title: Everything stated: no ask ops and no restated assumptions
reference: A two-zone public online store in Singapore for about 10,000 daily users: CDN, application load balancer, ECS, a MySQL-compatible database and object storage for images. The request names exposure, region, scale, availability and every tier, so there is nothing to ask; assumptions, if any, cover only things the user did not say.

turns.ask: Draw a public online store for about 10,000 daily users. Put it in Singapore only, a single region with two zones. Use ECS servers behind an application load balancer, a MySQL-compatible database, object storage for the product images and a CDN. There are no other requirements.

title: Answer to the question-first turn: the design appears and the question is not asked again
reference: Turn 1 asks and draws nothing. Turn 2 draws a public website on Alibaba Cloud in Singapore with a database, without asking again about exposure, region or traffic that the user just stated.

turns.ask: It is a public website for our customers, about 5,000 visitors a day, in Singapore, and it needs a database.

title: Flip the public-facing assumption to internal only
reference: Turn 1 draws the store with a public front door and shows an assumption chip (public-facing, alternative internal only). Turn 2 pins "internal only" as a requirement, removes the public entry path (CDN, ESA, public WAF) or replaces it with private access (VPN Gateway, Express Connect or an internal load balancer), and the public-facing chip is gone.

turns.ask: Build a web app for our online store in Singapore for about 10,000 daily users.
Change: Internal only instead of Public-facing

title: Just RDS for an app that runs on AWS
reference: Only the database on Alibaba Cloud: RDS in two zones in a VPC, linked to an other-cloud node labelled as the AWS app servers inside a group named AWS, through VPN Gateway (quick start) or Express Connect, optionally DTS. No application tier, load balancer or web server on Alibaba Cloud. Only the other-cloud node and its group carry the name AWS.

turns.ask: Just RDS for our app that runs on AWS.

title: RDS on Alibaba Cloud with DTS migration from AWS
reference: RDS PostgreSQL in two zones on Alibaba Cloud, an other-cloud node for the AWS database in an AWS group, a private link (VPN Gateway or Express Connect) and DTS for the migration and ongoing sync. No application tier on Alibaba Cloud.

turns.ask: Just RDS for our app on AWS. Migrate our existing PostgreSQL database from AWS RDS to it and keep it in sync for now.

title: Only WAF and CDN in front of a Google Cloud site
reference: The existing Google Cloud site is one other-cloud node inside a Google Cloud group. In front of it: Alibaba Cloud CDN and WAF (or ESA, which bundles both), with DNS for the domain. No compute, database or storage tier is redesigned. Only the other-cloud node and its group carry the name Google Cloud.

turns.ask: Only WAF and CDN in front of our Google Cloud site.

title: EC2 and S3 to be built on Alibaba Cloud still map to ECS and OSS
reference: Build-here request: EC2 becomes ECS and S3 becomes OSS in a normal Alibaba Cloud design. No other-cloud node, no AWS-named labels.

turns.ask: We want to use EC2 and S3 for our new app, built on Alibaba Cloud.

title: Load balancer and WAF in front of on-premises servers
reference: The on-premises servers are one on-premises node. In front of them on Alibaba Cloud: WAF with a load balancer (ALB or NLB), linked through VPN Gateway or Express Connect or a public-facing entry as the design suits, with DNS. No Alibaba Cloud compute tier.

turns.ask: Only a load balancer and WAF in front of our on-premises servers.

title: Online store with missing details (Korean)
reference: Same as the English case: a first diagram straight away, up to three assumptions and at most two questions with quick-reply options. Say, why, assumption and question text in Korean; product names as in the catalog.

turns.ask: 온라인 스토어용 웹 앱 구축해 주세요.

title: Just RDS for an app that runs on AWS (Korean)
reference: Same as the English case: RDS in two zones linked to an other-cloud node in an AWS group, no application tier. Text in Korean.

turns.ask: 저희 앱은 AWS에서 돌아가는데, RDS만 필요합니다.
